title: Ahava son of Rabbi Zeira
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs:
(Hyman writes: In the Yerushalmi he is called Achavo or Achava, or Achiya; and in the midrashim it was corrupted to the name "Acha son of Rabbi Zeira" [supplied ר״ז].)
He received Torah from his father, who lived in Caesarea in his father's place, where all were under the shadow of R' Abbahu, and he served there as the reciter (tanna), reciting baraitot, as in [Eruvin 96b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.96b.13-14) and [Rosh Hashanah 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.30b.10), where Rabbi Zeira [ר״ז] said to Ahava his son, "Go out and recite them"; and in [Rosh Hashanah 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.29a.17) and [Nedarim 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.32a.13), "Ahava son of Rabbi Zeira [ברי דר״ז] taught"; and in [Yerushalmi Pesachim 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.2.4.3), "R' Mana said: I went to Caesarea and heard R' Achavah bar Ze'ira say, etc." Hyman says the text was corrupted in [Yerushalmi Challah 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Challah.1.1.3), where "R' Mana said" reads "R' Achavah and Rabbi Zeira [ר״ז]," and he says it should read "bar Ze'ira."

He is mentioned in [Yerushalmi Berakhot 5:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.5.1.3), "R' Achava bar R"Z"; and there at the end of ch. 1, "They asked before R' Achava bar R"Z: How does your father conduct himself?"; and in [Yerushalmi Pesachim 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.1.1.7), followed in the supplied text by ב. And in [Yerushalmi Eruvin 6:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.6.7.2), "R' Acha bar R"Z."

And in [Bereshit Rabbah 39:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.39.11), "R' Achavah said in the name of R"Z," which Hyman says should read "bar Ze'ira."
And in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, parashat Acharei, "R' Berekhiah, brother of R"Z"; Hyman says it should read "R' Berekhiah and R' Achiya son of R"Z."

For [Tanchuma Noach 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma%2C_Noach.5.2) and Acharei §5, and Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 103b, the supplied transcription reads "in the name of R' Acha, R' Ze'ira." And so it is in [Vayikra Rabbah 26:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.26.4), "Rav Shalom in the name of R' Acha son of R"Z."
Hyman continues: And sometimes it was corrupted from Ahava to R' Abba, as in Bereshit Rabbah 84:2 (compare [Bereshit Rabbah 84:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.84.9)), where it reads "Ahava son of R"Z," and the statement is repeated in [Midrash Tehillim 28:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.28.4), where it reads "R' Abba b"Z"; and likewise in [Bereshit Rabbah 1:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.1.4), "Ahava b"Z," and the statement in Midrash Tehillim 90:12 (compare [Midrash Tehillim 90](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.90.7)) reads "R' Abbahu bar R"Z."
And we find Elazar bar Achavi in [Bereshit Rabbah 98:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.98.3); Hyman suggests that perhaps he is his son.[^7]

notes.text: R"Z abbreviation retained as printed; the Yerushalmi reading 'bar Ze'ira' in Hyman's own corrections suggests R. Ze'ira, but no registry expansion supplied. Variants Achavo/Achava/Achiya/Acha/Abba/Abbahu are Hyman's recorded forms. 'Ahava bari de-R"Z' kept as printed.

Printed citation labels (e.g., ה"ד, פכח-ד) are retained literally; Hyman's Hebrew chapter/halakha numbers are not converted to modern numbering. Whether 'ושם א"ר מנא' in unit p001 is a typographical or textual glitch is uncertain.

Source reads 'ר זעירא' without 'בר' in p004 (likely typographical omission); rendered literally as 'R. Ze'ira' with the omitted 'bar' noted. 'ב"ז' appears as printed (abbreviation of בר זעירא, uncertain).

Whole source/all notes reviewed. R.Mana says I WENT and HEARD (אזלית ושמעת), not You went. Tanna is the professional reciter of baraitot, not a claim about the Tannaitic generation. Hyman owns the Ahava/Achavo/Achava/Achiya/Acha/Abba/Abbahu identifications and proposed barZeira readings; his perhaps-son inference stays tentative. Full heading and repeated barZeira support contextual title, but no canonical identity merge. Extra ב. after Pes1:1 is retained as an unresolved locator, not proven page or folio2; p004 ר זעירא without bar remains literal and held. Prior citation-policy notes say no conversion although modern chapter numbers already appear: these are conventional numeral readings, not edition matching. Inherited notes retained; no typo-history assertion admitted. References to printed/native readings in inherited notes are preserved historical claims; this root pass uses supplied digital text and named saved editions, not a fresh pixel or correction-history verification.

The whole saved William Davidson Rosh Hashanah 30b paragraph explicitly writes Rabbi Zeira addressing Ahava his son and telling him to recite; this supports the corresponding local full father title and the reciter direction. The other uncollated abbreviated personal titles remain R' in this new English. Hyman’s variant identifications, corruption claims, father/teacher/residence narrative and the SHOULD READ emendations remain his claims, with their force preserved, rather than fresh manuscript or printed-source findings. The supplied extra ב. in p002 and ר זעירא without בר in p004 remain unresolved; p002 and p004 retain their holds. Mana’s I went/I heard, the genuine question about the father’s practice, all locators, variant spellings and the perhaps-son inference remain. The four current mixed notes remain verbatim, including their historical wording; no genealogy, teacher, chronology or canonical identity is admitted.

Rosh Hashanah 30b names R’ Zeira telling his son Ahava to recite a baraita. In Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 2:4, R’ Mana says that he went to Caesarea and heard Achava bar Zeira. The Guggenheimer Challah 1:1 gives Achava son of R’ Zeira, while the consulted Wikisource text has Achava and R’ Zeira as separate names. The printed Hyman notice (I, pp. 106–107) has Achiya in the question about his father’s practice. The exact textual locus for that quotation remains uncertain. The print also has the extra ב after the Pesachim 1:1 citation. Guggenheimer Pesachim 1:1 has Achava bar Zeira in the account of light in the ark, without settling the meaning of that extra letter. In the Tanchuma and Pesikta citation, Hyman’s print reads Acha bar Zeira where the supplied transcription omits bar. The consulted Tanchuma Noach 5 has Rav Achava bar Rav Zeira, and Vayikra Rabbah 26:4 has Rav Shalom citing R’ Acha son of R’ Zeira. The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 84:9 names Ahava bar Zeira and the parallel in Midrash Tehillim 28:4 names Abba bar Zeira. Bereshit Rabbah 1:4 names Ahava son of R’ Zeira for the teaching on repentance, while the consulted Wikisource Midrash Tehillim 90 has Abbahu without the patronymic in its parallel. The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 98:3 names Elazar ben Achui. Hyman’s account of how the spellings arose and his tentative identification of Elazar’s father remain his interpretations.

The linked Bavli passages show Zeira instructing his son to recite and Ahava transmitting baraitot. The linked Challah and Pesachim both give the patronymic, while older witnesses discussed above divide the names differently. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=252&lang=en) also compares the variants. Bereshit Rabbah 39:11 has Achavya speak in Rabbi Zeira’s name. Hyman proposes a patronymic. Elsewhere Bereshit Rabbah gives Ahava, while Midrash Tehillim gives Abba bar Zeira or, in the repentance passage, Abbahu without a patronymic. Hyman’s proposed family connection to Elazar remains tentative.
